project: Will it be possible to cure all cancers?
scientific_reframing: Can a candidate immune-recognition strategy support progressively stronger, indication-specific claims of durable cancer control after independent evidence of target selectivity, mechanism, heterogeneous coverage, escape resistance, safety, clinical durability, and replication?
main_conclusion: No current evidence establishes that one therapy can cure all cancers. Broad immune-recognition findings, including MR1-restricted T-cell receptor discovery work, are mechanistic hypotheses that require indication-specific evidence for coverage, dependence, escape, safety, durability, and replication before any clinical claim can be strengthened.
design_contribution: PAN-CURE provides noncompensatory decision gates and an S0-S4 evidence ladder that makes broad treatment claims auditable without converting discovery-stage evidence into universal-cure language.

independent_review_agent.reason: The deliverable is a static design-only research artifact with no code, public interface, security, persistence, or data-migration change; implementation self-check plus PDF validation was proportionate to risk.
